title: oddity-hunt-llm-failure-modes-notes
content:
TL;DR: quick personal log of ideas for an "oddity hunt" playbook — systematically surface small, repeatable LLM failure modes that matter in production (we miss these in macro benchmarks). Focus areas: hallucination boundary cases, KV-cache misbinds, prompt-sensitivity cliffs, subtle degenerations after long context, and failure combos (e.g., hallucination + toxic completion on rare tokens).

Why this: We have strong throughput/latency metrics but fewer small, reproducible buglets that actually cause customer incidents. A small targeted suite that finds brittle cases would improve model onboarding, rollout guardrails, and Optimize recommendations.

Goals:
- Build a repeatable probe suite that finds 1-2 new actionable failure classes per model version.
- Prioritize low-probability but high-impact failures (data privacy leak, instruction bypass, credential hallucination).
- Produce short repro cases (<=3-shot) that are human-verifiable and automatable.

Quick taxonomy (working):
1) Boundary hallucinations: model invents plausible but false facts when prompt slightly shifts. Example probe: ask about minor local businesses combined with obfuscated location phrasing.
2) KV-cache misbinds: token index corruption or context-stitching errors when using long context + incremental generation. Symptoms: repeats earlier unrelated context, or swaps entity attributes.
3) Prompt-sensitivity cliffs: tiny punctuation or stop-token changes cause large output difference. Good for regression tests.
4) Degeneration after long context: quality dips/failures after >8k tokens even if immediate prompt is short. Look for contradictions or sudden brevity.
5) Composition failures: multi-step tasks where intermediate step errors cascade (e.g., reasoning chain fails silently then final answer is confidently wrong).
6) Adversarial style transfer: model shifts style to user persona and leaks policy-violating phrasing when roleplay used.
7) Rare-token toxicity spikes: sequences that are benign except for rare-token triggers (emoji, unicode ligatures) that produce biased outputs.

Concrete probes to run (quick checklist):
- Micro A/B: single char changes (comma vs semicolon) in prompt preface. Run 100 seeds (nucleus sampling) and measure KL / answer drift.
- Locality manipulation: swap two entity mentions in long context window to see if attribution flips (KV-cache test).
- Interleaved tasking: create a 3-step chain where the 2nd step is noisy; check whether model propagates uncertainty or overconfidently asserts.
- Time-drift test: ask for dates relative to an anchor and then re-ask after inserting 4k tokens of irrelevant text; measure correctness.

Metrics (practical, automatable):
- Flip rate: fraction of paired prompts with different top-1 factual claims.
- Confident-false rate: scenarios where model assigns high probability/logit to an answer that is known false (we can approximate via reranking or model certainty proxies).
- Repro gap: consistency across seeds (high variance indicates brittle).
- Attribution-swap rate: in synthetic templates with two entities, frequency model swaps attributes.

Light experiment design (to run on dedicated or hosted small run):
- Dataset: 120 templates x 10 entity pairs x 5 shot/no-shot conditions x 5 seed draws = ~15k calls. Targeting medium-size model to enable many runs cheaply.
- Logging: record token-by-token probabilities + per-token KV cache hash (if accessible) + latency. Tag runs with model variant and quantization.
- Sanity check: include known-stable prompts (control) and known-failing prompts (from previous incidents).

Hypotheses and likely causes (notes):
- KV-cache misbinds often surface when using segmented contexts + piecemeal generation; our rerouting / caching heuristics might incorrectly index cache entries after truncation.
- Prompt-sensitivity cliffs may be due to tokenization boundary hitting important tokens (punctuation moves tokenization alignment). Small token align shifts can flip attention patterns.
- Degeneration after long context could be due to numeric precision/kv-eviction heuristics or attention matrix numerical drift in low-precision kernels.

Repro recipes (for each class produce 1-3 minimal repros):
- Boundary hallucination repro: 2-shot Q/A about a made-up local business 'The Gilded Sprocket' near an uncommon city name; then prepend 'Note: ignore prior context' and see if model contradicts itself.
- KV misbind repro: assemble context A (entity X attributes), context B (entity Y attributes), then ask about X after inserting 2k tokens of noise; measure attribute leakage.
- Prompt cliff repro: text with/without trailing period and with/without a soft stop token to see divergence.

Integration ideas for Redwood product surface:
- Redwood Optimize: add an "oddity-hunt" preset that runs quick probes on a model snapshot and generates a short human-readable report (3 repros + severity).
- Console: expose an "oddity alert" flag on rollouts; when toggled, automatically run probes during Canary. Fail rollout if confident-false rate > threshold.
- Dedicated/Private: provide a lightweight diagnostics endpoint that runs local probes (no data leaves customer infra).

Open questions / TODOs (actionable):
- [ ] Get access to token-prob logs for hosted models (Ethan to ping infra).
- [ ] Script templates for locality manipulation (Mika to draft).
- [ ] Decide thresholds for "confident-false" — is top1 entropy below X and contradicts ground truth? (need define).
- [ ] Run small pilot against three recent model snapshots (v1.9, v2.0a-quant, v2.0-8k).
- [ ] Add 10 real customer prompts (anonymized) to the probe suite to check for production relevance.

Notes to self: keep probes short and explainable. The goal isn't exhaustive adversarial search — it's to surface small brittle behaviors that are actionable for rollouts and quantization guidance. Prioritize tests that reproduce on multiple seeds and are easy to explain to PMs/CS.

References / brain dump (to curate):
- arXiv 2407.xxxx (attention drift / kv-cache ops) — linked above.
- Slack thread: #inference-oddities (thread id in linked_artifacts).
- Ethan's incident runbook: JIRA-INF-9213 (has two production repros for context-swap).
- Related PR: rv-experiments/pull/88 has a first-pass locality-swap harness.

Example minimal checklist for running locally:
1) clone rv-experiments, checkout branch oddity-hunt.
2) configure MODEL env to target canary snapshot.
3) run python probes/run_batch.py --template locality_swap --n_pairs 50 --seeds 5 --out csv.
4) inspect csv for attribution_swap_rate > 0.05. If >0.05, capture top 5 diffs and file a short ticket.

End notes: want to demo to Product in the 11/14 research sync — one slide + three short repros. Keep this document as the evolving scratchpad.

---
Personal micro-reflection: this feels like the type of work that is boring but massively high ROI — catches subtle regressions before customers do. Keep the experiments cheap and visible.
